summary: Alaska requires working smoke detectors in every home all the time, and CO detectors in homes with a fuel-burning appliance, an attached garage or carport, or a neighbouring parking space, but state law adds no special inspection or certificate when a house is sold.
alarmType: The statute says only that smoke detection devices must be of a type approved by the Alaska State Fire Marshal and installed the way the fire marshal approves. It does not itself name sealed 10-year batteries, hardwiring, interconnection or photoelectric sensing.
coAlarms: CO detection devices must be installed and maintained in every 'qualifying dwelling unit': one that contains or is served by a carbon-based fuel-burning appliance or device, has an attached garage or carport, or sits next to a parking space. The device must have an alarm and must be installed and maintained per the manufacturer's instructions. A CO-detector violation is a 'violation' rather than a misdemeanour under AS 18.70.100(c).
citation: AS 18.70.095 (smoke and carbon monoxide detection devices); penalty at AS 18.70.100
